crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: The AI Enablement Audit
children.blurb: The AI Enablement Audit is a structured review of an organization's readiness to deploy AI systems safely and lawfully.

children.name: Threat Modelling for Legal AI
children.blurb: Threat modelling for legal AI examines how a system that drafts, reviews, or researches legal content can fail in ways that harm clients, privilege, or case outcomes.

children.name: Data Loss Prevention and Sanitisation
children.blurb: Data loss prevention and sanitisation in AI security audits covers the controls that stop sensitive or regulated information from entering model training sets, prompts, retrieval contexts, or generated outputs.

children.name: Shadow AI in Legal Teams
children.blurb: Shadow AI in legal teams covers any AI tool or model that lawyers, paralegals, or legal operations staff use without formal approval from the firm's IT, security, or compliance function.

children.name: Bias Testing and Alignment
children.blurb: Bias testing and alignment covers evaluating model outputs for unfair treatment across protected attributes and checking whether model behavior matches organizational or legal expectations.

sections.body: This field examines how law firms and legal departments can safely bring AI tools into their work. It includes checking whether an AI system is fit for a specific legal task before it is used, looking for ways the model could be attacked or misled, preventing confidential client data from leaking out, finding unapproved AI use by staff, and testing whether outputs treat people unfairly. In practice, teams run structured reviews of vendor tools, simulate attacks on legal models, and scan outgoing data for privileged material. They also monitor network traffic and browser activity for signs of staff using consumer AI without permission. Bias testing involves running legal scenarios through a model and comparing results across protected characteristics.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts of this work are more mature than others. Data loss prevention has established tools for blocking sensitive patterns like client names or Social Security numbers, but they often miss paraphrased or embedded data. Threat modelling for legal models is still early because the models change quickly and attack methods are not standardized. Shadow AI detection is possible through network logs and browser extensions, but it cannot catch everything, especially on personal devices. Bias testing is repeatable for simple tasks like document review, but it is hard to define fairness for complex legal reasoning. The site tracks 142 active AI lawsuits, 92 of them intellectual property, which shows how unsettled the legal exposure is. No audit can guarantee safety, it can only reduce known risks.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The AI Enablement Audit is the starting point, giving a structured way to decide whether a legal AI tool is ready for a specific team. Threat Modelling for Legal AI then looks at how an approved model could be attacked or misused after deployment. Data Loss Prevention and Sanitisation covers the controls that keep client information from leaving through prompts, outputs, or training data. Shadow AI in Legal Teams addresses the risk that staff bypass these controls with unapproved tools. Bias Testing and Alignment checks whether the models that do get used produce unfair or misaligned results. A reader would start with the audit to understand scope, then move to threat modelling for security risks, data loss prevention for confidentiality, shadow AI for governance gaps, and bias testing for fairness.
